title: Prepared PDF design
intro: Design for the agreed preparation stage. Dark Start here nodes mark each graph's reading entry; numbered edges indicate ordering. These are workflow graphs, not a formal state model. Geometry and OCR remain later decisions.

groups.title: Assembly and handoff
groups.description: Explicit roles and page selections determine one ordinary prepared PDF.

groups.title: Originals and output publication
groups.description: A complete output becomes visible only at the no-clobber commit point.

discussion.title: Whole-page preservation and safe publication
discussion.summary: Define front → content → back, whole-page copying with explicit source gates, advisory versioned hints, staged graph validation and no overwrite. Dry-run runs all source checks. Link success fixes written/exit 0; later signals and reporting failures are warnings. The user confirmed single-quoted exclusions and ascending/descending ranges.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Source gates apply to dry-run and write; content is an assembly selection, not a page classification.
Show planned success, stream staging, copy-adapter validation and written success with post-commit warnings.

diagrams.title: Explicit roles become one prepared PDF
diagrams.caption: Design decision: selections retain argument order within roles, then front precedes content and back follows. Source preservation gates run in both dry-run and write. Content includes interior covers and conveys no book-page classification. The processor receives one PDF; optional role hints provide no geometry exemption.

diagrams.title: Publish a complete PDF without overwriting
diagrams.caption: Design decision: dry-run performs all source gates and stability checks, then reports planned without writing. The copy adapter validates the staged stream before publication. Defer SIGINT/SIGTERM across link and commit-state recording. A successful link fixes written/exit 0; caught later signals, cleanup and stdout failures are warnings, with stderr best effort if stdout is broken. SIGKILL can prevent reporting and leave a private .tmp name. Pre-commit failures preserve any prior destination. Sources are read-only throughout.
